text:
Kiefer Sherwood has 100 hits in 19 games. That number tells you most of what you need to know about how he plays, and why the Sharks wanted him. He's the undrafted American out of Miami (Ohio) who turned physical, honest minutes into a regular NHL job, and in San Jose he has taken Alexander Wennberg's spot beside Mason Marchment and Tyler Toffoli.

The scoring is lagging. Nine points in 19 games, but only two goals, and his shooting percentage (6.1%) is well below anything we'd expect to last. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows 52% of his shots come off the rush, and Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.6 wins last season, 79th among forwards. There's more scoring in him than this.

He has also been one of the louder voices in a hard month. He called out the Kings for "disrespectful" antics during a 6-2 loss, per Sportskeeda, and said the team's struggles aren't on the coaches, as Max Miller reported. Our range has him around 20 goals over a full season. Expect the goals to catch up.
headline: Sherwood brings the hits, and the honesty
